title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from previous pages): X = D_0 is a smooth (analytic or algebraic) space with a normal-crossings-type 'divisor at infinity'. In the intended application X is \bar M_{g,ν} or an étale chart of it. The divisor is not assumed to be a strict normal crossings divisor and may have self-intersecting branches (the nodal-curve example on the previous page). For d ≥ 0, D_d is the normalization of the d-fold crossing locus. D_d^! is the S_d-cover of D_d obtained by ordering the d local branches, so that D_d^!/S_d ≅ D_d. T_d = D_d^! ∧^{S_d} Z^d is a twisted rank-d lattice local system (183). G_d = T_d ⊗ G_m is the corresponding twisted relative torus over D_d (184).

This page does three things.

(1) T_d^! is the pullback of T_d to D_d^!, where it becomes the constant Z^d. S_d acts on it, and D_d^! → D_d is a Galois étale cover with group S_d.

(2) On D_d^! there are d maps s_i: D_d^! → D_1, one for each branch, sending a point to the i-th branch through it; S_d permutes them (185). D_1 → D_0 is a regular immersion of codimension 1 (an unramified immersion of the normalized divisor), so it has an invertible normal (or conormal) sheaf L_1 on D_1 (186). Pulling back gives d line bundles L_{d,i} = s_i^* L_1 on D_d^! (187). Each has an associated G_m-torsor L*_{d,i} of nonvanishing sections (188). Their fibre product P_d^! = ∏_i L*_{d,i} is a G_m^d-torsor (189).

(3) Since S_d permutes the L_{d,i}, it acts on P_d^! compatibly with its action on G_m^d by permuting factors. Descent (next page) gives a G_d-torsor P_d on D_d, and T_d is recovered as the local system of H_1 (equivalently π_1) of the fibres of P_d.

In modern terms, P_d is the punctured normal bundle (the algebraic 'deleted tubular neighbourhood') of the depth-d stratum. Its fibres are tori, and their fundamental group Z^d is the local inertia/monodromy lattice at that stratum.

Purpose: the next page restricts P_d to the open stratum D_d^* and takes its fundamental groupoid ΠP_d^*. This is meant to describe the 'structure at infinity' of the fundamental groupoid of M_{g,ν}: the boundary pieces, tangential base points, and the inertia tori Z^d attached to degenerations with d nodes. These pieces are then to be glued as d varies, via the correspondences D_d ← D_{d,d'} → D_{d'}.
errors: (188) says the torsor L*_{d,i} lives 'sur D_d', but the line bundle L_{d,i} lives on D_d^!, so the torsor should be on D_d^!. It only descends to D_d after taking the product and using the S_d-action, which is exactly what is done next.

If the parenthetical describing D_d^! → D_d really says 'connexe', that is not true in general. When the d branches lie on globally distinct components of the divisor, the S_d-cover is (partly) trivial and hence disconnected. What is true is that it is a Galois étale cover with group S_d and quotient D_d.
Normal versus conormal: the text first says 'faisceau normal', then (186) seems to read 'conormal'. The choice only changes the orientation (a sign) of the torsor, so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Ordered-branch S_d-cover D_d^! of the normalized d-fold stratum of a (non-strict) normal crossings divisor, with branch maps s_i to D_1
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of a normal crossings divisor by normalized strata and its monodromy cover (as in Deligne's Hodge II, and log-stratifications)
ideas.where_published: Closely related constructions appear in Grothendieck–Murre (LNM 208, 1971) on the tame fundamental group along a normal crossings divisor

ideas.what: G_d-torsor P_d built from the normal line bundles of the branches, whose fibres' H_1/π_1 is the inertia lattice T_d
ideas.modern_name: Punctured normal bundle / algebraic deleted tubular neighbourhood; the fibres of the Kato–Nakayama space are its real-torus analogue
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deformation to the normal cone (Fulton–MacPherson); tangential base points (Deligne 1989); log-geometric version (Kato–Nakayama 1999)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme mentions the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν} and tangential base points informally, without this construction

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of P_d restricted to the open stratum, as a building block of the structure at infinity of π_1(M_{g,ν})
ideas.modern_name: Boundary/tangential fundamental groupoids; log fundamental groups of boundary strata of moduli of curves

missed.claim: This is an explicit, purely algebraic (G_m-torsor) model of the boundary tubes of a normal crossings stratification, intended to describe the structure at infinity of the Teichmüller tower via fundamental groupoids. It anticipates the later log-geometric (Kato–Nakayama, log étale π_1) and tangential-base-point treatments. The construction itself, however, is standard today.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest: it documents how Grothendieck planned to make the 'structure à l'infini' in the Esquisse precise. It does not contain a result absent from the modern literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but standard foundational set-up (ordered-branch cover, normal torus torsor, inertia lattice). Its interest is historical, as Grothendieck's algebraic precursor to log/tangential-basepoint methods for the boundary of M_{g,ν}. No new result appears on this page.
transcription_corrections: The parenthetical after D_d^! is uncertain. It likely reads something like '(c'est un rev. galoisien/étale, (D_d^!, S_d) ≅ D_d)', i.e. a Galois cover whose quotient by S_d is D_d. The 'connexe' reading is doubtful.
The insertion between 'les' and 'morphismes' is 'd': 'on a les d morphismes'.
In (188), 'sur D_d' is as written by Grothendieck, but mathematically it should be D_d^! (his slip).
In the last line, 'il opère sur P_d' has a superscript '!' correction, giving 'P_d^!', and 'qui devient' is struck out and replaced by 'de façon compatible'.
